payload.question: Is this a possible leak or an instrumentation issue? Which pipeline section should an integrity engineer inspect first, and which sensors are unreliable?

cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.
verification_steps: Compare suspect instruments with independent observers and their actual received coverage.
Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

cards.title: Check common causes before counting independent corroboration

sources.boundary: Strong, possible, lower-threshold and noisy detections motivate multiscale inspection; not calibrated gas-pipeline attenuation.
sources.reference: User-provided public defense deck, not redistributed

sources.boundary: Motivates prior knowledge and source-quality review; gateway independence requires site instrumentation verification.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.
Independent gateways do not exclude an unrecorded shared power or operating cause.
verification_steps: Compare near, farther and weak/quiet connected observers jointly, not only above-threshold supporters.
Contrast a shared-path instrument with an independent observer; compare profiles, valid-sample overlap and graph distances.
Inspect contradictory or asynchronous changes rather than merging branch-level earliest/latest timings into a common onset.
Open applicable maintenance records and check effective revision and scope.

cards.title: Test operating transients as competing explanations

sources.boundary: Review of pressure methods, operating transients and model assumptions; not a site-specific operating procedure.

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. Compare the observed sign, timing and affected assets with an approved, incident-time-available record. A proposal is not an executed operation, and a superseded record is not current authority. Read the underlying records referenced by a coverage statement. A plausible explanation for one branch does not automatically explain a different pattern elsewhere. Incomplete logs cannot prove that no operation or leak occurred.
limitations: Temporal association is not a causal intervention.
The cited review includes liquid-pipeline methods; its parameters cannot be transferred directly to subsea gas.
cards.applies_when: Pressure changes could coincide with a valve, compressor, setpoint or calibration activity.
cards.review_basis: Research-grounded guidance; apply the current site operating procedure.
counterexamples: A broad positive operating shift does not by itself explain a separate localized negative region.
A real operating change can coexist with a leak or instrumentation fault.
verification_steps: Search affected and contrasting signal regions, not only the proposed inspection branch.
Open current records and distinguish planned, approved and executed activities.
Compare before/after periods near an observed change; note window censoring and retain missingness.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the numerical tool's actual method and retain its assumptions. The default method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours. On extended networks, a broad continuous pressure footprint may leave no unaffected neighbours or an overly wide bracket. The pressure-peak-focus fallback can then identify a priority inspection focus from the final five seconds of fully observed paired readings: a unique contiguous pressure-deficit peak, agreeing pairs, independent comparison paths and weaker immediately neighbouring stations whose contrast exceeds the baseline-noise allowance. Missing comparisons, tied/disconnected peaks, inadequate independence and excessive width still withhold a focus. Those comparison stations need not be unaffected. This is a spatial pressure-focus heuristic, not a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem or a guarantee that a physical leak lies inside the interval. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact leak coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or a research formula without its inputs. Physical intervention still requires the approved site procedure and operator authorization.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.
cards.applies_when: An engineer requests a leak location or an inspection recommendation from pressure observations.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived inspection guidance; confirm eligibility and site-specific hydraulic assumptions.
counterexamples: A larger pressure residual is not necessarily the nearest sensor to a leak.
Multiple disjoint pressure regions are not resolved by this single-leak bracket.
verification_steps: Check eligibility, paired coverage, observer independence, actual method and bounding comparisons.
State the priority interval and explain whether its neighbours are unaffected or simply weaker; do not call it a confidence interval or confirmed leak point.
Keep physical confirmation and operator authorization separate from the completed pressure-pattern assessment; do not clear alarms while waiting for an LLM.

cards.title: Expert-guided differential investigation program

sources.boundary: Architecture, expertise capture and open uncertainty/contradiction challenges; no subsea benchmark.

cards.guidance: Use this natural-language program to guide the existing read-only specialist workflow, not to assert an answer. Preserve competing leak, instrumentation and operating explanations. Select measurements and contextual checks that could distinguish them, including counterevidence. Apply only relevant knowledge, explicitly connect it to observed case evidence, and retain contradictions and missing prerequisites. Domain guidance supplies reasoning, not incident facts or authority to clear the numerical warning.
limitations: Inspired by DANA CAPTURE/APPLY and natural-language programs, not an OpenSSA or DanaOS implementation.
The paper's FinanceBench results do not establish pipeline diagnostic accuracy.
cards.applies_when: An anomaly episode requires a bounded, reviewable leak-versus-instrumentation RCA investigation.
cards.review_basis: DANA-inspired investigation program; apply site-reviewed expertise and operator approval.
counterexamples: Retrieving a relevant document without applying it is not RCA.
A well-cited but consistently wrong explanation is not successful expert reasoning.
verification_steps: Quality: establish what was measured reliably and what remains missing.
Diagnosis: inspect connectivity, independent domains and competing signal regions.
Diagnosis: choose relevant operational records and discriminating comparisons.
Response: explain which guidance was applied, supporting and contradicting case evidence, and remaining gaps.
Critic: check case facts and knowledge citations against their original pinned sources.
Handoff: request qualified engineer verification; unresolved evidence remains unresolved.

payload.text:
Decision
Work P6 first on the integrity-review track: its strongest joint pressure loss supports a suspected integrity incident. Use the accepted 800-1200 m inspection priority along P6, around stations ST5 and ST6. Distance along the pipe is called chainage. This pressure-focus interval is not a confirmed leak point or dispatch approval [claim-114; KN-LOCALIZATION-R1]. Keep P7 on the shared-connection instrumentation track and P2 on the operating-transition/process track; neither has a supported joint leak pattern in this window.

Your first actions
1. Scope the read-only P6 integrity review to the accepted interval, retaining ST4 and ST7 as weaker bounding comparisons rather than treating the whole pressure footprint as the leak source.
2. Put gateway-P7-0, the shared data connection for both sensors at ST1, ST3, ST5 and ST7, on the instrumentation-review track. Use the opened calibration record and stable comparison path; do not label eight separate hardware failures.
3. Use the opened P2 pressure-setting record to classify its broad rise as a matching transition, not a new pressure loss. Keep any change beyond its recorded period distinct.
4. Seek independent physical pressure and flow confirmation for the P6 focus, and a reference outside gateway-P7-0 for P7. These checks distinguish real pressure loss from a shifted measurement path without changing controls.

Already checked
The specialists compared synchronized profiles, paired sensors at the same stations, and shared connections, and opened the operating and calibration records. P6-ST5-A was 1.425 bar below its supplied typical-pressure reference in the final five seconds; P6-ST6-A was 1.432 bar below it. Bar is a pressure unit. Nearby P6-ST4-A and P6-ST7-A were only 0.394 and 0.393 bar below their own references. The peak sensors' losses persisted for 59 seconds, from 91 to 150 seconds elapsed in the recording [ev-178; ev-182; ev-174; ev-186]. These baseline-relative deficits are distinct from the already-completed before/after comparisons.

Why this decision
P6's agreeing pressure pattern spans two shared connections, whereas P7's large persistent offsets follow one connection and match the calibration context. The suspect P7 readings are P7-ST1-A/B, P7-ST3-A/B, P7-ST5-A/B and P7-ST7-A/B: they shifted downward to another level, not a flatline. Hardware faults are not established. P6 screening spike flags do not establish unreliable instruments when the reviewed profiles show coherent pressure changes [comparison calls; KN-QUALITY-R1; KN-INDEPENDENCE-R1]. All 6,720 expected samples were usable, with no identified missing or invalid readings, but the health review was partial: complete coverage does not certify every sensor [ev-225].

What changes the decision
Independent P6 confirmation or deterioration strengthens its integrity priority. Sustained P7 loss outside its shared connection, or a new P2 departure beyond the logged transition, changes those branches' tracks. The opened logs are incomplete; the P2 operation does not explain P6's negative focus [LOG-EXTENDED-COVERAGE-001; OP-P2-EXTENDED-001; KN-OPERATING-R1].

cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.
verification_steps: Compare suspect instruments with independent observers and their actual received coverage.
Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

cards.title: Check common causes before counting independent corroboration

sources.boundary: Strong, possible, lower-threshold and noisy detections motivate multiscale inspection; not calibrated gas-pipeline attenuation.
sources.reference: User-provided public defense deck, not redistributed

sources.boundary: Motivates prior knowledge and source-quality review; gateway independence requires site instrumentation verification.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.
Independent gateways do not exclude an unrecorded shared power or operating cause.
verification_steps: Compare near, farther and weak/quiet connected observers jointly, not only above-threshold supporters.
Contrast a shared-path instrument with an independent observer; compare profiles, valid-sample overlap and graph distances.
Inspect contradictory or asynchronous changes rather than merging branch-level earliest/latest timings into a common onset.
Open applicable maintenance records and check effective revision and scope.

cards.title: Test operating transients as competing explanations

sources.boundary: Review of pressure methods, operating transients and model assumptions; not a site-specific operating procedure.

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. Compare the observed sign, timing and affected assets with an approved, incident-time-available record. A proposal is not an executed operation, and a superseded record is not current authority. Read the underlying records referenced by a coverage statement. A plausible explanation for one branch does not automatically explain a different pattern elsewhere. Incomplete logs cannot prove that no operation or leak occurred.
limitations: Temporal association is not a causal intervention.
The cited review includes liquid-pipeline methods; its parameters cannot be transferred directly to subsea gas.
cards.applies_when: Pressure changes could coincide with a valve, compressor, setpoint or calibration activity.
cards.review_basis: Research-grounded guidance; apply the current site operating procedure.
counterexamples: A broad positive operating shift does not by itself explain a separate localized negative region.
A real operating change can coexist with a leak or instrumentation fault.
verification_steps: Search affected and contrasting signal regions, not only the proposed inspection branch.
Open current records and distinguish planned, approved and executed activities.
Compare before/after periods near an observed change; note window censoring and retain missingness.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the numerical tool's actual method and retain its assumptions. The default method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours. On extended networks, a broad continuous pressure footprint may leave no unaffected neighbours or an overly wide bracket. The pressure-peak-focus fallback can then identify a priority inspection focus from the final five seconds of fully observed paired readings: a unique contiguous pressure-deficit peak, agreeing pairs, independent comparison paths and weaker immediately neighbouring stations whose contrast exceeds the baseline-noise allowance. Missing comparisons, tied/disconnected peaks, inadequate independence and excessive width still withhold a focus. Those comparison stations need not be unaffected. This is a spatial pressure-focus heuristic, not a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem or a guarantee that a physical leak lies inside the interval. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact leak coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or a research formula without its inputs. Physical intervention still requires the approved site procedure and operator authorization.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.
cards.applies_when: An engineer requests a leak location or an inspection recommendation from pressure observations.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived inspection guidance; confirm eligibility and site-specific hydraulic assumptions.
counterexamples: A larger pressure residual is not necessarily the nearest sensor to a leak.
Multiple disjoint pressure regions are not resolved by this single-leak bracket.
verification_steps: Check eligibility, paired coverage, observer independence, actual method and bounding comparisons.
State the priority interval and explain whether its neighbours are unaffected or simply weaker; do not call it a confidence interval or confirmed leak point.
Keep physical confirmation and operator authorization separate from the completed pressure-pattern assessment; do not clear alarms while waiting for an LLM.

sources.boundary: Architecture, expertise capture and open uncertainty/contradiction challenges; no subsea benchmark.

Domain guidance supplies reasoning, not incident facts or authority to clear the numerical warning.

ENGINEER QUESTION
Is this a possible leak or an instrumentation issue? Which pipeline section should an integrity engineer inspect first, and which sensors are unreliable?
ENGINEERING ASSESSMENT
Decision
Work P6 first on the integrity-review track: its strongest joint pressure loss supports a suspected integrity incident. Use the accepted 800-1200 m inspection priority along P6, around stations ST5 and ST6. Distance along the pipe is called chainage. This pressure-focus interval is not a confirmed leak point or dispatch approval [claim-114; KN-LOCALIZATION-R1]. Keep P7 on the shared-connection instrumentation track and P2 on the operating-transition/process track; neither has a supported joint leak pattern in this window.

Your first actions
1. Scope the read-only P6 integrity review to the accepted interval, retaining ST4 and ST7 as weaker bounding comparisons rather than treating the whole pressure footprint as the leak source.
2. Put gateway-P7-0, the shared data connection for both sensors at ST1, ST3, ST5 and ST7, on the instrumentation-review track. Use the opened calibration record and stable comparison path; do not label eight separate hardware failures.
3. Use the opened P2 pressure-setting record to classify its broad rise as a matching transition, not a new pressure loss. Keep any change beyond its recorded period distinct.
4. Seek independent physical pressure and flow confirmation for the P6 focus, and a reference outside gateway-P7-0 for P7. These checks distinguish real pressure loss from a shifted measurement path without changing controls.

Already checked
The specialists compared synchronized profiles, paired sensors at the same stations, and shared connections, and opened the operating and calibration records. P6-ST5-A was 1.425 bar below its supplied typical-pressure reference in the final five seconds; P6-ST6-A was 1.432 bar below it. Bar is a pressure unit. Nearby P6-ST4-A and P6-ST7-A were only 0.394 and 0.393 bar below their own references. The peak sensors' losses persisted for 59 seconds, from 91 to 150 seconds elapsed in the recording [ev-178; ev-182; ev-174; ev-186]. These baseline-relative deficits are distinct from the already-completed before/after comparisons.

Why this decision
P6's agreeing pressure pattern spans two shared connections, whereas P7's large persistent offsets follow one connection and match the calibration context. The suspect P7 readings are P7-ST1-A/B, P7-ST3-A/B, P7-ST5-A/B and P7-ST7-A/B: they shifted downward to another level, not a flatline. Hardware faults are not established. P6 screening spike flags do not establish unreliable instruments when the reviewed profiles show coherent pressure changes [comparison calls; KN-QUALITY-R1; KN-INDEPENDENCE-R1]. All 6,720 expected samples were usable, with no identified missing or invalid readings, but the health review was partial: complete coverage does not certify every sensor [ev-225].

What changes the decision
Independent P6 confirmation or deterioration strengthens its integrity priority. Sustained P7 loss outside its shared connection, or a new P2 departure beyond the logged transition, changes those branches' tracks. The opened logs are incomplete; the P2 operation does not explain P6's negative focus [LOG-EXTENDED-COVERAGE-001; OP-P2-EXTENDED-001; KN-OPERATING-R1].

ENGINEER QUESTION
Is this a possible leak or an instrumentation issue? Which pipeline section should an integrity engineer inspect first, and which sensors are unreliable?
ENGINEERING ASSESSMENT
Decision
Work P6 first on the integrity-review track: its strongest joint pressure loss supports a suspected integrity incident. Use the accepted 800-1200 m inspection priority along P6, around stations ST5 and ST6. Distance along the pipe is called chainage. This pressure-focus interval is not a confirmed leak point or dispatch approval [claim-114; KN-LOCALIZATION-R1]. Keep P7 on the shared-connection instrumentation track and P2 on the operating-transition/process track; neither has a supported joint leak pattern in this window.

Your first actions
1. Scope the read-only P6 integrity review to the accepted interval, retaining ST4 and ST7 as weaker bounding comparisons rather than treating the whole pressure footprint as the leak source.
2. Put gateway-P7-0, the shared data connection for both sensors at ST1, ST3, ST5 and ST7, on the instrumentation-review track. Use the opened calibration record and stable comparison path; do not label eight separate hardware failures.
3. Use the opened P2 pressure-setting record to classify its broad rise as a matching transition, not a new pressure loss. Keep any change beyond its recorded period distinct.
4. Seek independent physical pressure and flow confirmation for the P6 focus, and a reference outside gateway-P7-0 for P7. These checks distinguish real pressure loss from a shifted measurement path without changing controls.

Already checked
The specialists compared synchronized profiles, paired sensors at the same stations, and shared connections, and opened the operating and calibration records. P6-ST5-A was 1.425 bar below its supplied typical-pressure reference in the final five seconds; P6-ST6-A was 1.432 bar below it. Bar is a pressure unit. Nearby P6-ST4-A and P6-ST7-A were only 0.394 and 0.393 bar below their own references. The peak sensors' losses persisted for 59 seconds, from 91 to 150 seconds elapsed in the recording [ev-178; ev-182; ev-174; ev-186]. These baseline-relative deficits are distinct from the already-completed before/after comparisons.

Why this decision
P6's agreeing pressure pattern spans two shared connections, whereas P7's large persistent offsets follow one connection and match the calibration context. The suspect P7 readings are P7-ST1-A/B, P7-ST3-A/B, P7-ST5-A/B and P7-ST7-A/B: they shifted downward to another level, not a flatline. Hardware faults are not established. P6 screening spike flags do not establish unreliable instruments when the reviewed profiles show coherent pressure changes [comparison calls; KN-QUALITY-R1; KN-INDEPENDENCE-R1]. All 6,720 expected samples were usable, with no identified missing or invalid readings, but the health review was partial: complete coverage does not certify every sensor [ev-225].

What changes the decision
Independent P6 confirmation or deterioration strengthens its integrity priority. Sustained P7 loss outside its shared connection, or a new P2 departure beyond the logged transition, changes those branches' tracks. The opened logs are incomplete; the P2 operation does not explain P6's negative focus [LOG-EXTENDED-COVERAGE-001; OP-P2-EXTENDED-001; KN-OPERATING-R1].

leak (possible): P6 has the strongest supported joint negative pressure pattern: both sensors at ST5 and ST6 lose about 1.38-1.39 bar in the reviewed before/after comparison, across two shared connections, with smaller changes at neighbouring stations. This supports prioritizing a suspected integrity incident, not confirming its physical cause. The accepted 800-1200 m interval is a spatial pressure-focus heuristic, not hydraulic leak localization or a confidence interval. P2's positive operating transition does not explain this separate negative region, but incomplete logs and unexcluded shared operating or measurement causes remain counterevidence to certainty. Independent pressure and flow confirmation at the P6 focus is the discriminating physical check; advisory guidance does not authorize intervention.

payload.question: Is this a possible leak or an instrumentation issue? Which pipeline section should an integrity engineer inspect first, and which sensors are unreliable?

cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.
verification_steps: Compare suspect instruments with independent observers and their actual received coverage.
Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

cards.title: Check common causes before counting independent corroboration

sources.boundary: Strong, possible, lower-threshold and noisy detections motivate multiscale inspection; not calibrated gas-pipeline attenuation.
sources.reference: User-provided public defense deck, not redistributed

sources.boundary: Motivates prior knowledge and source-quality review; gateway independence requires site instrumentation verification.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.
Independent gateways do not exclude an unrecorded shared power or operating cause.
verification_steps: Compare near, farther and weak/quiet connected observers jointly, not only above-threshold supporters.
Contrast a shared-path instrument with an independent observer; compare profiles, valid-sample overlap and graph distances.
Inspect contradictory or asynchronous changes rather than merging branch-level earliest/latest timings into a common onset.
Open applicable maintenance records and check effective revision and scope.

cards.title: Test operating transients as competing explanations

sources.boundary: Review of pressure methods, operating transients and model assumptions; not a site-specific operating procedure.

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. Compare the observed sign, timing and affected assets with an approved, incident-time-available record. A proposal is not an executed operation, and a superseded record is not current authority. Read the underlying records referenced by a coverage statement. A plausible explanation for one branch does not automatically explain a different pattern elsewhere. Incomplete logs cannot prove that no operation or leak occurred.
limitations: Temporal association is not a causal intervention.
The cited review includes liquid-pipeline methods; its parameters cannot be transferred directly to subsea gas.
cards.applies_when: Pressure changes could coincide with a valve, compressor, setpoint or calibration activity.
cards.review_basis: Research-grounded guidance; apply the current site operating procedure.
counterexamples: A broad positive operating shift does not by itself explain a separate localized negative region.
A real operating change can coexist with a leak or instrumentation fault.
verification_steps: Search affected and contrasting signal regions, not only the proposed inspection branch.
Open current records and distinguish planned, approved and executed activities.
Compare before/after periods near an observed change; note window censoring and retain missingness.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the numerical tool's actual method and retain its assumptions. The default method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours. On extended networks, a broad continuous pressure footprint may leave no unaffected neighbours or an overly wide bracket. The pressure-peak-focus fallback can then identify a priority inspection focus from the final five seconds of fully observed paired readings: a unique contiguous pressure-deficit peak, agreeing pairs, independent comparison paths and weaker immediately neighbouring stations whose contrast exceeds the baseline-noise allowance. Missing comparisons, tied/disconnected peaks, inadequate independence and excessive width still withhold a focus. Those comparison stations need not be unaffected. This is a spatial pressure-focus heuristic, not a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem or a guarantee that a physical leak lies inside the interval. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact leak coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or a research formula without its inputs. Physical intervention still requires the approved site procedure and operator authorization.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.
cards.applies_when: An engineer requests a leak location or an inspection recommendation from pressure observations.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived inspection guidance; confirm eligibility and site-specific hydraulic assumptions.
counterexamples: A larger pressure residual is not necessarily the nearest sensor to a leak.
Multiple disjoint pressure regions are not resolved by this single-leak bracket.
verification_steps: Check eligibility, paired coverage, observer independence, actual method and bounding comparisons.
State the priority interval and explain whether its neighbours are unaffected or simply weaker; do not call it a confidence interval or confirmed leak point.
Keep physical confirmation and operator authorization separate from the completed pressure-pattern assessment; do not clear alarms while waiting for an LLM.

Diagnosis: choose relevant operational records and discriminating comparisons.

cards.guidance: Use this natural-language program to guide the existing read-only specialist workflow, not to assert an answer. Preserve competing leak, instrumentation and operating explanations. Select measurements and contextual checks that could distinguish them, including counterevidence. Apply only relevant knowledge, explicitly connect it to observed case evidence, and retain contradictions and missing prerequisites. Domain guidance supplies reasoning, not incident facts or authority to clear the numerical warning.
limitations: Inspired by DANA CAPTURE/APPLY and natural-language programs, not an OpenSSA or DanaOS implementation.
The paper's FinanceBench results do not establish pipeline diagnostic accuracy.
cards.applies_when: An anomaly episode requires a bounded, reviewable leak-versus-instrumentation RCA investigation.
cards.review_basis: DANA-inspired investigation program; apply site-reviewed expertise and operator approval.
counterexamples: Retrieving a relevant document without applying it is not RCA.
A well-cited but consistently wrong explanation is not successful expert reasoning.
verification_steps: Quality: establish what was measured reliably and what remains missing.
Diagnosis: inspect connectivity, independent domains and competing signal regions.
Diagnosis: choose relevant operational records and discriminating comparisons.
Response: explain which guidance was applied, supporting and contradicting case evidence, and remaining gaps.
Critic: check case facts and knowledge citations against their original pinned sources.
Handoff: request qualified engineer verification; unresolved evidence remains unresolved.

payload.question: Is this a possible leak or an instrumentation issue? Which pipeline section should an integrity engineer inspect first, and which sensors are unreliable?

cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.
verification_steps: Compare suspect instruments with independent observers and their actual received coverage.
Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

cards.title: Check common causes before counting independent corroboration

sources.boundary: Strong, possible, lower-threshold and noisy detections motivate multiscale inspection; not calibrated gas-pipeline attenuation.
sources.reference: User-provided public defense deck, not redistributed

sources.boundary: Motivates prior knowledge and source-quality review; gateway independence requires site instrumentation verification.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.
Independent gateways do not exclude an unrecorded shared power or operating cause.
verification_steps: Compare near, farther and weak/quiet connected observers jointly, not only above-threshold supporters.
Contrast a shared-path instrument with an independent observer; compare profiles, valid-sample overlap and graph distances.
Inspect contradictory or asynchronous changes rather than merging branch-level earliest/latest timings into a common onset.
Open applicable maintenance records and check effective revision and scope.

cards.title: Test operating transients as competing explanations

sources.boundary: Review of pressure methods, operating transients and model assumptions; not a site-specific operating procedure.

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. Compare the observed sign, timing and affected assets with an approved, incident-time-available record. A proposal is not an executed operation, and a superseded record is not current authority. Read the underlying records referenced by a coverage statement. A plausible explanation for one branch does not automatically explain a different pattern elsewhere. Incomplete logs cannot prove that no operation or leak occurred.
limitations: Temporal association is not a causal intervention.
The cited review includes liquid-pipeline methods; its parameters cannot be transferred directly to subsea gas.
cards.applies_when: Pressure changes could coincide with a valve, compressor, setpoint or calibration activity.
cards.review_basis: Research-grounded guidance; apply the current site operating procedure.
counterexamples: A broad positive operating shift does not by itself explain a separate localized negative region.
A real operating change can coexist with a leak or instrumentation fault.
verification_steps: Search affected and contrasting signal regions, not only the proposed inspection branch.
Open current records and distinguish planned, approved and executed activities.
Compare before/after periods near an observed change; note window censoring and retain missingness.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the numerical tool's actual method and retain its assumptions. The default method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours. On extended networks, a broad continuous pressure footprint may leave no unaffected neighbours or an overly wide bracket. The pressure-peak-focus fallback can then identify a priority inspection focus from the final five seconds of fully observed paired readings: a unique contiguous pressure-deficit peak, agreeing pairs, independent comparison paths and weaker immediately neighbouring stations whose contrast exceeds the baseline-noise allowance. Missing comparisons, tied/disconnected peaks, inadequate independence and excessive width still withhold a focus. Those comparison stations need not be unaffected. This is a spatial pressure-focus heuristic, not a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem or a guarantee that a physical leak lies inside the interval. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact leak coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or a research formula without its inputs. Physical intervention still requires the approved site procedure and operator authorization.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.
cards.applies_when: An engineer requests a leak location or an inspection recommendation from pressure observations.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived inspection guidance; confirm eligibility and site-specific hydraulic assumptions.
counterexamples: A larger pressure residual is not necessarily the nearest sensor to a leak.
Multiple disjoint pressure regions are not resolved by this single-leak bracket.
verification_steps: Check eligibility, paired coverage, observer independence, actual method and bounding comparisons.
State the priority interval and explain whether its neighbours are unaffected or simply weaker; do not call it a confidence interval or confirmed leak point.
Keep physical confirmation and operator authorization separate from the completed pressure-pattern assessment; do not clear alarms while waiting for an LLM.

For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.

No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.

cards.title: Test operating transients as competing explanations

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the numerical tool's actual method and retain its assumptions. The default method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours. On extended networks, a broad continuous pressure footprint may leave no unaffected neighbours or an overly wide bracket. The pressure-peak-focus fallback can then identify a priority inspection focus from the final five seconds of fully observed paired readings: a unique contiguous pressure-deficit peak, agreeing pairs, independent comparison paths and weaker immediately neighbouring stations whose contrast exceeds the baseline-noise allowance. Missing comparisons, tied/disconnected peaks, inadequate independence and excessive width still withhold a focus. Those comparison stations need not be unaffected. payload.question: Is this a possible leak or an instrumentation issue? Which pipeline section should an integrity engineer inspect first, and which sensors are unreliable?

cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.
verification_steps: Compare suspect instruments with independent observers and their actual received coverage.
Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

cards.title: Check common causes before counting independent corroboration

sources.boundary: Strong, possible, lower-threshold and noisy detections motivate multiscale inspection; not calibrated gas-pipeline attenuation.
sources.reference: User-provided public defense deck, not redistributed

sources.boundary: Motivates prior knowledge and source-quality review; gateway independence requires site instrumentation verification.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.

cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.
Independent gateways do not exclude an unrecorded shared power or operating cause.

cards.title: Test operating transients as competing explanations

sources.boundary: Review of pressure methods, operating transients and model assumptions; not a site-specific operating procedure.

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. Compare the observed sign, timing and affected assets with an approved, incident-time-available record. A proposal is not an executed operation, and a superseded record is not current authority. Read the underlying records referenced by a coverage statement. A plausible explanation for one branch does not automatically explain a different pattern elsewhere. Incomplete logs cannot prove that no operation or leak occurred.
limitations: Temporal association is not a causal intervention.
The cited review includes liquid-pipeline methods; its parameters cannot be transferred directly to subsea gas.
cards.applies_when: Pressure changes could coincide with a valve, compressor, setpoint or calibration activity.
cards.review_basis: Research-grounded guidance; apply the current site operating procedure.
counterexamples: A broad positive operating shift does not by itself explain a separate localized negative region.
A real operating change can coexist with a leak or instrumentation fault.
verification_steps: Search affected and contrasting signal regions, not only the proposed inspection branch.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the numerical tool's actual method and retain its assumptions. The default method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours. On extended networks, a broad continuous pressure footprint may leave no unaffected neighbours or an overly wide bracket. The pressure-peak-focus fallback can then identify a priority inspection focus from the final five seconds of fully observed paired readings: a unique contiguous pressure-deficit peak, agreeing pairs, independent comparison paths and weaker immediately neighbouring stations whose contrast exceeds the baseline-noise allowance. Missing comparisons, tied/disconnected peaks, inadequate independence and excessive width still withhold a focus. Those comparison stations need not be unaffected. This is a spatial pressure-focus heuristic, not a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem or a guarantee that a physical leak lies inside the interval. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact leak coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or a research formula without its inputs. Physical intervention still requires the approved site procedure and operator authorization.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.

Multiple disjoint pressure regions are not resolved by this single-leak bracket.

Decision
Work P6 first on the integrity-review track: its supported inspection priority is 800–1200 m along the pipe, around stations P6-ST5/ST6. This is a suspected integrity incident, not a confirmed leak point or dispatch approval; the accepted pressure-focus method brackets a measured peak, not hydraulic coordinates [claim-113, claim-114, KN-LOCALIZATION-R1]. Next prioritize P7's gateway-P7-0 on the instrumentation track. Keep P2 on process review, with a separate P2-ST3-A instrument check; route P1, P3, P4 and P5 to the specific reading checks below rather than additional leak inspections.

Your first actions
1. Scope the read-only P6 integrity review to the accepted interval and retain ST4/ST7 as weaker bounding comparisons [claim-114, KN-LOCALIZATION-R1].
2. Keep P7-ST1/ST3/ST5/ST7 A/B readings together under gateway-P7-0, their shared data connection; use the reviewed calibration record to distinguish its offset from independent pressure evidence [MAINT-P7-GW-002].
3. Use the already-matched P2 pressure-setting record for the 90–145-second elapsed period to separate that transition from a new loss; retain P2-ST3-A's brief spikes as a separate issue [OP-P2-EXTENDED-001].
4. Seek independent physical pressure/flow confirmation around P6-ST5/ST6 and confirmation of gateway assignments before attributing a cause or considering intervention [KN-INDEPENDENCE-R1, KN-LOCALIZATION-R1].

Already checked
Specialists compared synchronized profiles, paired sensors—two sensors at each station—and operating records. P6-ST5-A remained 1.40 bar below the supplied typical-pressure reference during seconds 355–360, versus 0.38 bar at ST4-A; bar is a pressure unit [ev-178, ev-174]. The paired peak spans two gateways and persists through the final 60 seconds. Smaller P6 outer-station changes accompany the pattern, but their relationship remains unresolved; they are not separate leak diagnoses [claim-113, 8ecdea2c-d57e-57a5-b846-1c17cd401b6f].

Why this decision
Concrete suspect readings are P1-ST6-A's gradual upward drift, P3-ST7-A's downward drift, P2-ST3-A and P4-ST7-B's two brief spikes each, P3-ST7-B's single brief spike, and P5-ST8-B's flatline after 180 seconds. Their comparison partners are not thereby faulty. P7's odd-station readings show a shared persistent offset, not eight established hardware faults. P6 screening spike counts do not establish unreliable readings: its profiles show coherent pressure changes [8ecdea2c-d57e-57a5-b846-1c17cd401b6f, 850b6ee6-c724-5764-806b-383320933b44, ev-091, KN-QUALITY-R1]. Coverage is 99.18%, but P1-ST7-B and P3-ST5-B each lack 20 of 60 readings; P4-ST8-A received 60 with 15 invalid and only 45 usable. Health review is partial [ev-225, ev-027, ev-083, ev-125].

What changes the decision
Escalate the review priority if P6 deteriorates, independent P7 readings outside the shared connection sustain a loss, or P2 changes beyond its documented transition. The operating excerpt is incomplete; independent physical confirmation remains necessary, but does not postpone the supported P6 desk-review priority [LOG-EXTENDED-COVERAGE-001].

These current values and the synchronized rise support process review with no supported joint leak pattern in this window, not a safety clearance. P2-ST3-A separately has two brief spikes outside the coherent transition interpretation, while ST3-B is its comparison partner rather than an identified faulty instrument [ev-041, 8ecdea2c-d57e-57a5-b846-1c17cd401b6f, KN-QUALITY-R1]. Independent pressure/flow evidence or a sustained departure beyond the documented operating period would distinguish a new event from the already-matched transition.

cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.
verification_steps: Compare suspect instruments with independent observers and their actual received coverage.
Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

cards.title: Check common causes before counting independent corroboration

sources.boundary: Strong, possible, lower-threshold and noisy detections motivate multiscale inspection; not calibrated gas-pipeline attenuation.
sources.reference: User-provided public defense deck, not redistributed

sources.boundary: Motivates prior knowledge and source-quality review; gateway independence requires site instrumentation verification.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.
Independent gateways do not exclude an unrecorded shared power or operating cause.
verification_steps: Compare near, farther and weak/quiet connected observers jointly, not only above-threshold supporters.
Contrast a shared-path instrument with an independent observer; compare profiles, valid-sample overlap and graph distances.
Inspect contradictory or asynchronous changes rather than merging branch-level earliest/latest timings into a common onset.
Open applicable maintenance records and check effective revision and scope.

cards.title: Test operating transients as competing explanations

sources.boundary: Review of pressure methods, operating transients and model assumptions; not a site-specific operating procedure.

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. Compare the observed sign, timing and affected assets with an approved, incident-time-available record. A proposal is not an executed operation, and a superseded record is not current authority. Read the underlying records referenced by a coverage statement. A plausible explanation for one branch does not automatically explain a different pattern elsewhere. Incomplete logs cannot prove that no operation or leak occurred.
limitations: Temporal association is not a causal intervention.
The cited review includes liquid-pipeline methods; its parameters cannot be transferred directly to subsea gas.
cards.applies_when: Pressure changes could coincide with a valve, compressor, setpoint or calibration activity.
cards.review_basis: Research-grounded guidance; apply the current site operating procedure.
counterexamples: A broad positive operating shift does not by itself explain a separate localized negative region.
A real operating change can coexist with a leak or instrumentation fault.
verification_steps: Search affected and contrasting signal regions, not only the proposed inspection branch.
Open current records and distinguish planned, approved and executed activities.
Compare before/after periods near an observed change; note window censoring and retain missingness.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the numerical tool's actual method and retain its assumptions. The default method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours. On extended networks, a broad continuous pressure footprint may leave no unaffected neighbours or an overly wide bracket. The pressure-peak-focus fallback can then identify a priority inspection focus from the final five seconds of fully observed paired readings: a unique contiguous pressure-deficit peak, agreeing pairs, independent comparison paths and weaker immediately neighbouring stations whose contrast exceeds the baseline-noise allowance. Missing comparisons, tied/disconnected peaks, inadequate independence and excessive width still withhold a focus. Those comparison stations need not be unaffected. This is a spatial pressure-focus heuristic, not a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem or a guarantee that a physical leak lies inside the interval. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact leak coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or a research formula without its inputs. Physical intervention still requires the approved site procedure and operator authorization.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.
cards.applies_when: An engineer requests a leak location or an inspection recommendation from pressure observations.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived inspection guidance; confirm eligibility and site-specific hydraulic assumptions.
counterexamples: A larger pressure residual is not necessarily the nearest sensor to a leak.
Multiple disjoint pressure regions are not resolved by this single-leak bracket.
verification_steps: Check eligibility, paired coverage, observer independence, actual method and bounding comparisons.
State the priority interval and explain whether its neighbours are unaffected or simply weaker; do not call it a confidence interval or confirmed leak point.
Keep physical confirmation and operator authorization separate from the completed pressure-pattern assessment; do not clear alarms while waiting for an LLM.

cards.title: Expert-guided differential investigation program

sources.boundary: Architecture, expertise capture and open uncertainty/contradiction challenges; no subsea benchmark.

cards.guidance: Use this natural-language program to guide the existing read-only specialist workflow, not to assert an answer. Preserve competing leak, instrumentation and operating explanations. Select measurements and contextual checks that could distinguish them, including counterevidence. Apply only relevant knowledge, explicitly connect it to observed case evidence, and retain contradictions and missing prerequisites. Domain guidance supplies reasoning, not incident facts or authority to clear the numerical warning.
limitations: Inspired by DANA CAPTURE/APPLY and natural-language programs, not an OpenSSA or DanaOS implementation.
The paper's FinanceBench results do not establish pipeline diagnostic accuracy.

cards.review_basis: DANA-inspired investigation program; apply site-reviewed expertise and operator approval.
counterexamples: Retrieving a relevant document without applying it is not RCA.

payload.public_output:
ENGINEER QUESTION
Is this a possible leak or an instrumentation issue? Which pipeline section should an integrity engineer inspect first, and which sensors are unreliable?
ENGINEERING ASSESSMENT
Decision
Work P6 first on the integrity-review track: its supported inspection priority is 800–1200 m along the pipe, around stations P6-ST5/ST6. This is a suspected integrity incident, not a confirmed leak point or dispatch approval; the accepted pressure-focus method brackets a measured peak, not hydraulic coordinates [claim-113, claim-114, KN-LOCALIZATION-R1]. Next prioritize P7's gateway-P7-0 on the instrumentation track. Keep P2 on process review, with a separate P2-ST3-A instrument check; route P1, P3, P4 and P5 to the specific reading checks below rather than additional leak inspections.

Your first actions
1. Scope the read-only P6 integrity review to the accepted interval and retain ST4/ST7 as weaker bounding comparisons [claim-114, KN-LOCALIZATION-R1].
2. Keep P7-ST1/ST3/ST5/ST7 A/B readings together under gateway-P7-0, their shared data connection; use the reviewed calibration record to distinguish its offset from independent pressure evidence [MAINT-P7-GW-002].
3. Use the already-matched P2 pressure-setting record for the 90–145-second elapsed period to separate that transition from a new loss; retain P2-ST3-A's brief spikes as a separate issue [OP-P2-EXTENDED-001].
4. Seek independent physical pressure/flow confirmation around P6-ST5/ST6 and confirmation of gateway assignments before attributing a cause or considering intervention [KN-INDEPENDENCE-R1, KN-LOCALIZATION-R1].

Already checked
Executed comparisons cover synchronized profiles, paired sensors—two sensors at each station—and the recorded operating period. For elapsed seconds 355–360, P6-ST5-A's final-five-second summary deficit against the supplied normal-pressure reference was 1.40 bar, versus 0.38 bar at ST4-A; bar is a pressure unit. These are period summaries, not exact deficits at every sample or completed field verification [ev-178, ev-174]. The paired peak spans two gateways, and screening establishes persistence through the final 60 seconds. Smaller P6 outer-station changes accompany the pressure-event footprint, but their relationship to the suspected source remains unresolved; they are not separate leak diagnoses [claim-113, 8ecdea2c-d57e-57a5-b846-1c17cd401b6f].

Why this decision
Concrete suspect readings are P1-ST6-A's gradual upward drift, P3-ST7-A's downward drift, P2-ST3-A and P4-ST7-B's brief spikes, and P5-ST8-B's flatline after 180 seconds. P3-ST7-B has one screening spike flag requiring verification, but its reviewed profile shows a modest coherent pressure shift, not an established isolated spike or unreliable reading. Comparison partners are not faulty merely because their paired sensor is suspect. P7's odd-station readings show a shared persistent offset, not eight established hardware faults. P6 screening spike counts likewise do not establish unreliable readings: its profiles show coherent pressure changes [8ecdea2c-d57e-57a5-b846-1c17cd401b6f, 850b6ee6-c724-5764-806b-383320933b44, ev-091, KN-QUALITY-R1]. Coverage is 99.18%, but P1-ST7-B and P3-ST5-B each lack 20 of 60 readings; P4-ST8-A received 60 with 15 invalid and only 45 usable. Health review is partial, so coverage does not establish every instrument's reliability [ev-225, ev-027, ev-083, ev-125].

What changes the decision
Reassess the review priority if P6 deteriorates, independent P7 readings outside the shared connection sustain a loss, or P2 changes beyond its documented transition. The operating excerpt is incomplete; independent physical confirmation remains necessary, but does not postpone the supported P6 desk-review priority [LOG-EXTENDED-COVERAGE-001].
Sources: claim-113, claim-114, KN-LOCALIZATION-R1, KN-INDEPENDENCE-R1, KN-QUALITY-R1, MAINT-P7-GW-002, OP-P2-EXTENDED-001, LOG-EXTENDED-COVERAGE-001, ev-178, ev-174, 8ecdea2c-d57e-57a5-b846-1c17cd401b6f, 850b6ee6-c724-5764-806b-383320933b44, ev-091, ev-225, ev-027, ev-083, ev-125
COMPETING EXPLANATIONS
leak (possible): P6 supports a possible leak-pattern investigation because agreeing station pairs show a sustained negative pressure region, strongest at ST5/ST6 and weaker at ST4/ST7, across two measurement connections [claim-113, 8ecdea2c-d57e-57a5-b846-1c17cd401b6f, KN-INDEPENDENCE-R1]. The observed onset develops after 90 elapsed seconds, and the final measurements remain below the supplied normal reference; this is not merely a detector label. The positive P2 operating transition does not explain this separate negative region. Pressure evidence does not establish the physical cause, and the incomplete operating excerpt leaves competing actions unknown. Independent local pressure and flow confirmation should test the integrity interpretation; the accepted interval remains an inspection priority only [claim-114, KN-LOCALIZATION-R1].
Sources: claim-113, claim-114, 8ecdea2c-d57e-57a5-b846-1c17cd401b6f, subsea_064302943e35406696de0f918c811eb2, LOG-EXTENDED-COVERAGE-001, KN-INDEPENDENCE-R1, KN-LOCALIZATION-R1
instrumentation or telemetry (possible): P7 has concrete shared-path evidence: every other station's A/B readings step down near 90 elapsed seconds and remain shifted, matching the named calibration connection and approximate negative offset [850b6ee6-c724-5764-806b-383320933b44, MAINT-P7-GW-002]. This supports checking gateway-P7-0, not declaring all eight sensors faulty; quieter ST2 readings on the other gateway contradict an independent, uniformly broad pressure loss. Work P6 first on the integrity-review track: its supported inspection priority is 800–1200 m along the pipe, around stations P6-ST5/ST6. Your first actions

2. Keep P7-ST1/ST3/ST5/ST7 A/B readings together under gateway-P7-0, their shared data connection; use the reviewed calibration record to distinguish its offset from independent pressure evidence [MAINT-P7-GW-002].

Executed comparisons cover synchronized profiles, paired sensors—two sensors at each station—and the recorded operating period. Concrete suspect readings are P1-ST6-A's gradual upward drift, P3-ST7-A's downward drift, P2-ST3-A and P4-ST7-B's brief spikes, and P5-ST8-B's flatline after 180 seconds. Reassess the review priority if P6 deteriorates, independent P7 readings outside the shared connection sustain a loss, or P2 changes beyond its documented transition. The operating excerpt is incomplete; independent physical confirmation remains necessary, but does not postpone the supported P6 desk-review priority [LOG-EXTENDED-COVERAGE-001].
