Decision
Work P6 first on the integrity-review track: its supported inspection priority is 800–1200 m along the pipe, around stations P6-ST5/ST6. This is a suspected integrity incident, not a confirmed leak point or dispatch approval; the accepted pressure-focus method brackets a measured peak, not hydraulic coordinates [claim-113, claim-114, KN-LOCALIZATION-R1]. Next prioritize P7's gateway-P7-0 on the instrumentation track. Keep P2 on process review, with a separate P2-ST3-A instrument check; route P1, P3, P4 and P5 to the specific reading checks below rather than additional leak inspections.

Your first actions
1. Scope the read-only P6 integrity review to the accepted interval and retain ST4/ST7 as weaker bounding comparisons [claim-114, KN-LOCALIZATION-R1].
2. Keep P7-ST1/ST3/ST5/ST7 A/B readings together under gateway-P7-0, their shared data connection; use the reviewed calibration record to distinguish its offset from independent pressure evidence [MAINT-P7-GW-002].
3. Use the already-matched P2 pressure-setting record for the 90–145-second elapsed period to separate that transition from a new loss; retain P2-ST3-A's brief spikes as a separate issue [OP-P2-EXTENDED-001].
4. Seek independent physical pressure/flow confirmation around P6-ST5/ST6 and confirmation of gateway assignments before attributing a cause or considering intervention [KN-INDEPENDENCE-R1, KN-LOCALIZATION-R1].

Already checked
Executed comparisons cover synchronized profiles, paired sensors—two sensors at each station—and the recorded operating period. For elapsed seconds 355–360, P6-ST5-A's final-five-second summary deficit against the supplied normal-pressure reference was 1.40 bar, versus 0.38 bar at ST4-A; bar is a pressure unit. These are period summaries, not exact deficits at every sample or completed field verification [ev-178, ev-174]. The paired peak spans two gateways, and screening establishes persistence through the final 60 seconds. Smaller P6 outer-station changes accompany the pressure-event footprint, but their relationship to the suspected source remains unresolved; they are not separate leak diagnoses [claim-113, 8ecdea2c-d57e-57a5-b846-1c17cd401b6f].

Why this decision
Concrete suspect readings are P1-ST6-A's gradual upward drift, P3-ST7-A's downward drift, P2-ST3-A and P4-ST7-B's brief spikes, and P5-ST8-B's flatline after 180 seconds. P3-ST7-B has one screening spike flag requiring verification, but its reviewed profile shows a modest coherent pressure shift, not an established isolated spike or unreliable reading. Comparison partners are not faulty merely because their paired sensor is suspect. P7's odd-station readings show a shared persistent offset, not eight established hardware faults. P6 screening spike counts likewise do not establish unreliable readings: its profiles show coherent pressure changes [8ecdea2c-d57e-57a5-b846-1c17cd401b6f, 850b6ee6-c724-5764-806b-383320933b44, ev-091, KN-QUALITY-R1]. Coverage is 99.18%, but P1-ST7-B and P3-ST5-B each lack 20 of 60 readings; P4-ST8-A received 60 with 15 invalid and only 45 usable. Health review is partial, so coverage does not establish every instrument's reliability [ev-225, ev-027, ev-083, ev-125].

What changes the decision
Reassess the review priority if P6 deteriorates, independent P7 readings outside the shared connection sustain a loss, or P2 changes beyond its documented transition. The operating excerpt is incomplete; independent physical confirmation remains necessary, but does not postpone the supported P6 desk-review priority [LOG-EXTENDED-COVERAGE-001].

The observed onset develops after 90 elapsed seconds, and the final measurements remain below the supplied normal reference; this is not merely a detector label. The positive P2 operating transition does not explain this separate negative region. cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.
verification_steps: Compare suspect instruments with independent observers and their actual received coverage.
Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

cards.title: Check common causes before counting independent corroboration

sources.boundary: Strong, possible, lower-threshold and noisy detections motivate multiscale inspection; not calibrated gas-pipeline attenuation.
sources.reference: User-provided public defense deck, not redistributed

sources.boundary: Motivates prior knowledge and source-quality review; gateway independence requires site instrumentation verification.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.
Independent gateways do not exclude an unrecorded shared power or operating cause.
verification_steps: Compare near, farther and weak/quiet connected observers jointly, not only above-threshold supporters.
Contrast a shared-path instrument with an independent observer; compare profiles, valid-sample overlap and graph distances.
Inspect contradictory or asynchronous changes rather than merging branch-level earliest/latest timings into a common onset.
Open applicable maintenance records and check effective revision and scope.

cards.title: Test operating transients as competing explanations

sources.boundary: Review of pressure methods, operating transients and model assumptions; not a site-specific operating procedure.

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. Read the underlying records referenced by a coverage statement. A plausible explanation for one branch does not automatically explain a different pattern elsewhere. Incomplete logs cannot prove that no operation or leak occurred.
limitations: Temporal association is not a causal intervention.

cards.applies_when: Pressure changes could coincide with a valve, compressor, setpoint or calibration activity.
cards.review_basis: Research-grounded guidance; apply the current site operating procedure.
counterexamples: A broad positive operating shift does not by itself explain a separate localized negative region.

verification_steps: Search affected and contrasting signal regions, not only the proposed inspection branch.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the numerical tool's actual method and retain its assumptions. The default method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours. On extended networks, a broad continuous pressure footprint may leave no unaffected neighbours or an overly wide bracket. The pressure-peak-focus fallback can then identify a priority inspection focus from the final five seconds of fully observed paired readings: a unique contiguous pressure-deficit peak, agreeing pairs, independent comparison paths and weaker immediately neighbouring stations whose contrast exceeds the baseline-noise allowance. Missing comparisons, tied/disconnected peaks, inadequate independence and excessive width still withhold a focus. Those comparison stations need not be unaffected. This is a spatial pressure-focus heuristic, not a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem or a guarantee that a physical leak lies inside the interval. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact leak coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or a research formula without its inputs. Physical intervention still requires the approved site procedure and operator authorization.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.
cards.applies_when: An engineer requests a leak location or an inspection recommendation from pressure observations.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived inspection guidance; confirm eligibility and site-specific hydraulic assumptions.
counterexamples: A larger pressure residual is not necessarily the nearest sensor to a leak.
Multiple disjoint pressure regions are not resolved by this single-leak bracket.
verification_steps: Check eligibility, paired coverage, observer independence, actual method and bounding comparisons.
State the priority interval and explain whether its neighbours are unaffected or simply weaker; do not call it a confidence interval or confirmed leak point.
Keep physical confirmation and operator authorization separate from the completed pressure-pattern assessment; do not clear alarms while waiting for an LLM.

payload.purpose: assess_event_and_location
payload.question: Is this a possible leak or an instrumentation issue? Which pipeline section should an integrity engineer inspect first, and which sensors are unreliable?

cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.
verification_steps: Compare suspect instruments with independent observers and their actual received coverage.
Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

cards.title: Check common causes before counting independent corroboration

sources.boundary: Strong, possible, lower-threshold and noisy detections motivate multiscale inspection; not calibrated gas-pipeline attenuation.
sources.reference: User-provided public defense deck, not redistributed

sources.boundary: Motivates prior knowledge and source-quality review; gateway independence requires site instrumentation verification.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.
Independent gateways do not exclude an unrecorded shared power or operating cause.
verification_steps: Compare near, farther and weak/quiet connected observers jointly, not only above-threshold supporters.
Contrast a shared-path instrument with an independent observer; compare profiles, valid-sample overlap and graph distances.
Inspect contradictory or asynchronous changes rather than merging branch-level earliest/latest timings into a common onset.
Open applicable maintenance records and check effective revision and scope.

cards.title: Test operating transients as competing explanations

sources.boundary: Review of pressure methods, operating transients and model assumptions; not a site-specific operating procedure.

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. Compare the observed sign, timing and affected assets with an approved, incident-time-available record. A proposal is not an executed operation, and a superseded record is not current authority. Read the underlying records referenced by a coverage statement. A plausible explanation for one branch does not automatically explain a different pattern elsewhere. Incomplete logs cannot prove that no operation or leak occurred.
limitations: Temporal association is not a causal intervention.
The cited review includes liquid-pipeline methods; its parameters cannot be transferred directly to subsea gas.
cards.applies_when: Pressure changes could coincide with a valve, compressor, setpoint or calibration activity.
cards.review_basis: Research-grounded guidance; apply the current site operating procedure.
counterexamples: A broad positive operating shift does not by itself explain a separate localized negative region.
A real operating change can coexist with a leak or instrumentation fault.
verification_steps: Search affected and contrasting signal regions, not only the proposed inspection branch.
Open current records and distinguish planned, approved and executed activities.
Compare before/after periods near an observed change; note window censoring and retain missingness.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the numerical tool's actual method and retain its assumptions. The default method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours. On extended networks, a broad continuous pressure footprint may leave no unaffected neighbours or an overly wide bracket. The pressure-peak-focus fallback can then identify a priority inspection focus from the final five seconds of fully observed paired readings: a unique contiguous pressure-deficit peak, agreeing pairs, independent comparison paths and weaker immediately neighbouring stations whose contrast exceeds the baseline-noise allowance. Missing comparisons, tied/disconnected peaks, inadequate independence and excessive width still withhold a focus. Those comparison stations need not be unaffected. This is a spatial pressure-focus heuristic, not a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem or a guarantee that a physical leak lies inside the interval. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact leak coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or a research formula without its inputs. Physical intervention still requires the approved site procedure and operator authorization.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.
cards.applies_when: An engineer requests a leak location or an inspection recommendation from pressure observations.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived inspection guidance; confirm eligibility and site-specific hydraulic assumptions.
counterexamples: A larger pressure residual is not necessarily the nearest sensor to a leak.
Multiple disjoint pressure regions are not resolved by this single-leak bracket.
verification_steps: Check eligibility, paired coverage, observer independence, actual method and bounding comparisons.
State the priority interval and explain whether its neighbours are unaffected or simply weaker; do not call it a confidence interval or confirmed leak point.
Keep physical confirmation and operator authorization separate from the completed pressure-pattern assessment; do not clear alarms while waiting for an LLM.

cards.title: Expert-guided differential investigation program

sources.boundary: Architecture, expertise capture and open uncertainty/contradiction challenges; no subsea benchmark.

cards.guidance: Use this natural-language program to guide the existing read-only specialist workflow, not to assert an answer. Preserve competing leak, instrumentation and operating explanations. Select measurements and contextual checks that could distinguish them, including counterevidence. Apply only relevant knowledge, explicitly connect it to observed case evidence, and retain contradictions and missing prerequisites. Domain guidance supplies reasoning, not incident facts or authority to clear the numerical warning.
limitations: Inspired by DANA CAPTURE/APPLY and natural-language programs, not an OpenSSA or DanaOS implementation.
The paper's FinanceBench results do not establish pipeline diagnostic accuracy.
cards.applies_when: An anomaly episode requires a bounded, reviewable leak-versus-instrumentation RCA investigation.
cards.review_basis: DANA-inspired investigation program; apply site-reviewed expertise and operator approval.
counterexamples: Retrieving a relevant document without applying it is not RCA.
A well-cited but consistently wrong explanation is not successful expert reasoning.
verification_steps: Quality: establish what was measured reliably and what remains missing.
Diagnosis: inspect connectivity, independent domains and competing signal regions.
Diagnosis: choose relevant operational records and discriminating comparisons.
Response: explain which guidance was applied, supporting and contradicting case evidence, and remaining gaps.
Critic: check case facts and knowledge citations against their original pinned sources.
Handoff: request qualified engineer verification; unresolved evidence remains unresolved.

sources.boundary: Review of pressure methods, operating transients and model assumptions; not a site-specific operating procedure.

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. Compare the observed sign, timing and affected assets with an approved, incident-time-available record. A proposal is not an executed operation, and a superseded record is not current authority. Read the underlying records referenced by a coverage statement. A plausible explanation for one branch does not automatically explain a different pattern elsewhere. The cited review includes liquid-pipeline methods; its parameters cannot be transferred directly to subsea gas.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the numerical tool's actual method and retain its assumptions. The default method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours. On extended networks, a broad continuous pressure footprint may leave no unaffected neighbours or an overly wide bracket. The pressure-peak-focus fallback can then identify a priority inspection focus from the final five seconds of fully observed paired readings: a unique contiguous pressure-deficit peak, agreeing pairs, independent comparison paths and weaker immediately neighbouring stations whose contrast exceeds the baseline-noise allowance. Missing comparisons, tied/disconnected peaks, inadequate independence and excessive width still withhold a focus. Those comparison stations need not be unaffected. This is a spatial pressure-focus heuristic, not a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem or a guarantee that a physical leak lies inside the interval. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact leak coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or a research formula without its inputs. Physical intervention still requires the approved site procedure and operator authorization.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.
cards.applies_when: An engineer requests a leak location or an inspection recommendation from pressure observations.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived inspection guidance; confirm eligibility and site-specific hydraulic assumptions.
counterexamples: A larger pressure residual is not necessarily the nearest sensor to a leak.
Multiple disjoint pressure regions are not resolved by this single-leak bracket.
verification_steps: Check eligibility, paired coverage, observer independence, actual method and bounding comparisons.
State the priority interval and explain whether its neighbours are unaffected or simply weaker; do not call it a confidence interval or confirmed leak point.
Keep physical confirmation and operator authorization separate from the completed pressure-pattern assessment; do not clear alarms while waiting for an LLM.

cards.title: Expert-guided differential investigation program

sources.boundary: Architecture, expertise capture and open uncertainty/contradiction challenges; no subsea benchmark.

cards.guidance: Use this natural-language program to guide the existing read-only specialist workflow, not to assert an answer. Preserve competing leak, instrumentation and operating explanations. Select measurements and contextual checks that could distinguish them, including counterevidence. Apply only relevant knowledge, explicitly connect it to observed case evidence, and retain contradictions and missing prerequisites. Domain guidance supplies reasoning, not incident facts or authority to clear the numerical warning.
limitations: Inspired by DANA CAPTURE/APPLY and natural-language programs, not an OpenSSA or DanaOS implementation.
The paper's FinanceBench results do not establish pipeline diagnostic accuracy.
cards.applies_when: An anomaly episode requires a bounded, reviewable leak-versus-instrumentation RCA investigation.
cards.review_basis: DANA-inspired investigation program; apply site-reviewed expertise and operator approval.
counterexamples: Retrieving a relevant document without applying it is not RCA.

verification_steps: Quality: establish what was measured reliably and what remains missing.
Diagnosis: inspect connectivity, independent domains and competing signal regions.
Diagnosis: choose relevant operational records and discriminating comparisons.
Response: explain which guidance was applied, supporting and contradicting case evidence, and remaining gaps.

Decision
Work first on P7's shared data connection, gateway-P7-0, serving both sensors at stations ST1, ST3, ST5 and ST7: this belongs on the instrumentation track, not a pipeline leak-inspection track. P2 belongs on the process-review track; P1-ST6-A, P3-ST7-A, P4-ST7-B and P6-ST3-A need individual instrument checks, with P6-ST8-B also showing a current flatline. P4-ST8-A and missing P1/P3 readings need coverage attention. P5 has no supported joint leak pattern in this window. No pipeline section has a qualified inspection interval: the strongest negative group lacks independent observers because its eight taps share one connection [ev-230; PROC-EXTENDED-001; KN-LOCALIZATION-R1].

Your first actions
1. Keep P7-ST1/ST3/ST5/ST7 on the shared-connection review track, using the accepted calibration record and already-compared ST2 pair to scope the reading-offset review.
2. Use OP-P2-EXTENDED-001 to classify P2's broad positive shift as an operating-transition review, not a new joint pressure-loss priority.
3. Flag the named drifting, spiking, flatlining and incomplete instruments for read-only measurement-quality review; keep their stable comparison partners separate.
4. Seek independent pressure and flow confirmation outside gateway-P7-0 to distinguish a real pressure loss from a conversion offset before any physical inspection decision.

Already checked
The specialists compared paired sensors, time profiles and connection assignments, and opened the operating and calibration records. P7-ST1-A is 0.749 bar below the supplied typical-pressure reference in the final five seconds; ST2-A is 0.060 bar above it. Bar is a pressure unit. The shared P7 readings shift down about 0.75 bar near 90 seconds elapsed in the recording, matching the calibration record's sign, size and timing [ev-194; ev-198; 06d703c8-9870-5125-a94c-09c3aefa6e47; MAINT-P7-GW-002].

Why this decision
P2's paired rises match the recorded approximately 0.4-bar transition from 90 to 145 seconds; its ST1-A returns to within 0.003 bar of the supplied reference in the final five seconds [ev-034; OP-P2-EXTENDED-001]. Aggregate usable coverage is 99.18%, but P1-ST7-B and P3-ST5-B each lack 20 of 60 readings; P4-ST8-A has 15 invalid received readings and only 45 usable. The health review is partial, so high coverage does not establish universal reliability [ev-225; ev-027; ev-083; ev-125].

What changes the decision
A sustained independently measured P7 pressure loss outside the shared connection, deterioration of the P3 paired station rather than its A sensor alone, or a new P2 loss beyond the recorded transition would change the review priority. These observations support measurement and process checks now, not confirmed hardware faults, a physical leak location or clearance. The supplied normal reference is not field verification, and the opened logs are incomplete [LOG-EXTENDED-COVERAGE-001; KN-QUALITY-R1; KN-INDEPENDENCE-R1].

answer.text:
Decision
Work first on P7's shared data connection, gateway-P7-0, serving both sensors at stations ST1, ST3, ST5 and ST7: prioritize instrumentation review, not pipeline leak inspection. Next, keep P2 on the process-review track. P1-ST6-A, P3-ST7-A, P4-ST7-B and P6-ST3-A need individual instrument checks; P6-ST8-B needs a flatline check. P4-ST8-A and incomplete P1/P3 readings need coverage attention. P5's reviewed ST1 pair is close to the supplied typical-pressure reference; retain contextual pressure review, not a separate leak priority based on that pair. This is not branch-wide clearance [ev-130; ev-132]. No qualified inspection interval is available: P7's strongest negative group lacks independent corroboration because its eight taps share one connection [ev-230; KN-LOCALIZATION-R1].

Your first actions
1. Keep both sensors at P7-ST1/ST3/ST5/ST7 on the shared-connection track; use the accepted calibration record and already-compared ST2 pair to scope the reading-offset review.
2. Use OP-P2-EXTENDED-001 to separate P2's recorded positive transition from any new pressure-loss finding.
3. Flag the named drifting, spiking, flatlining and incomplete instruments for read-only measurement-quality review; keep stable comparison partners separate.
4. Seek independent pressure and flow confirmation outside gateway-P7-0 to distinguish physical pressure loss from a conversion offset before a physical inspection decision.

Already checked
Specialists compared paired sensors, time profiles and connection assignments and opened the operating and calibration records. P7-ST1-A is 0.749 bar below the supplied typical-pressure reference in the final five seconds; ST2-A is 0.060 bar above it. Bar is a pressure unit. The shared P7 readings step down about 0.75 bar near 90 seconds elapsed in the recording, matching the calibration record's sign, size and timing [ev-194; ev-198; 06d703c8-9870-5125-a94c-09c3aefa6e47; MAINT-P7-GW-002].

Why this decision
P2's paired rises match the recorded approximately 0.4-bar transition from 90 to 145 seconds; ST1-A finishes 0.002 bar below the supplied reference [ev-034; OP-P2-EXTENDED-001]. Aggregate usable coverage is 99.18%, but P1-ST7-B and P3-ST5-B each lack 20 of 60 readings. P4-ST8-A has 15 invalid received readings, leaving 45 usable. The health review is partial: aggregate coverage does not establish every instrument's reliability [ev-225; ev-027; ev-083; ev-125; KN-QUALITY-R1].

What changes the decision
Sustained independently measured P7 pressure loss outside the shared connection, deterioration involving both P3-ST7 sensors rather than A alone, or a new P2 loss beyond the recorded transition would change the priority. Current findings support measurement and process review, not confirmed hardware faults or a physical leak location. The supplied reference is not field verification, and the opened logs are incomplete [ca47940c-5314-5223-9458-d811871f3164; LOG-EXTENDED-COVERAGE-001; KN-INDEPENDENCE-R1].

competing_causes.text: The P7 evidence supports a shared measurement-offset explanation: both sensors at four every-other stations move down together on gateway-P7-0, while the compared ST2 pair on gateway-P7-1 stays stable. The approximately 0.75-bar step matches the revised calibration record, but that association does not confirm a hardware fault or make eight connected taps independent evidence. Separately, individual drifting readings, brief spikes and a current flatline support targeted measurement checks. An independent pressure reference outside the shared conversion connection would distinguish measurement bias from a physical loss.

P2's positive paired pressure shift spans both gateway groups and matches the opened record's expected approximately 0.4-bar rise and 90-to-145-second operating period. Representative final-five-second summaries return close to the supplied typical-pressure reference: ST1-A is 0.002 bar below it, while ST1-B and ST8 A/B are slightly above it. This supports an operating-context explanation for P2 rather than a new joint pressure-loss priority. KN-OPERATING-R1 requires retaining competing causes because timing agreement is not causal proof, and the log excerpt is incomplete. Independent operating-state confirmation remains useful if pressure changes outside the recorded period.

In the compared P7 and P3 groups, there is no supported joint leak pattern in this window. P7's large negative readings follow one shared conversion connection, while the compared ST2 pair on a different connection remains stable; P3-ST7-A's negative drift is contradicted by its stable paired sensor. P2 instead shows a positive transition matching its opened operating record. These contrasts support different measurement and process attention tracks, not a window-wide exclusion of leaks. A concurrent leak cannot be excluded, but that uncertainty is not a positive integrity finding or grounds for inventing an inspection interval; sustained independent pressure loss with supporting flow evidence would warrant reconsidering the priority.

cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.
verification_steps: Compare suspect instruments with independent observers and their actual received coverage.
Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

cards.title: Check common causes before counting independent corroboration

sources.boundary: Strong, possible, lower-threshold and noisy detections motivate multiscale inspection; not calibrated gas-pipeline attenuation.
sources.reference: User-provided public defense deck, not redistributed

sources.boundary: Motivates prior knowledge and source-quality review; gateway independence requires site instrumentation verification.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.
Independent gateways do not exclude an unrecorded shared power or operating cause.
verification_steps: Compare near, farther and weak/quiet connected observers jointly, not only above-threshold supporters.
Contrast a shared-path instrument with an independent observer; compare profiles, valid-sample overlap and graph distances.
Inspect contradictory or asynchronous changes rather than merging branch-level earliest/latest timings into a common onset.
Open applicable maintenance records and check effective revision and scope.

cards.title: Test operating transients as competing explanations

sources.boundary: Review of pressure methods, operating transients and model assumptions; not a site-specific operating procedure.

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. Compare the observed sign, timing and affected assets with an approved, incident-time-available record. A proposal is not an executed operation, and a superseded record is not current authority. Read the underlying records referenced by a coverage statement. A plausible explanation for one branch does not automatically explain a different pattern elsewhere. Incomplete logs cannot prove that no operation or leak occurred.
limitations: Temporal association is not a causal intervention.
The cited review includes liquid-pipeline methods; its parameters cannot be transferred directly to subsea gas.
cards.applies_when: Pressure changes could coincide with a valve, compressor, setpoint or calibration activity.
cards.review_basis: Research-grounded guidance; apply the current site operating procedure.
counterexamples: A broad positive operating shift does not by itself explain a separate localized negative region.
A real operating change can coexist with a leak or instrumentation fault.
verification_steps: Search affected and contrasting signal regions, not only the proposed inspection branch.
Open current records and distinguish planned, approved and executed activities.
Compare before/after periods near an observed change; note window censoring and retain missingness.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the numerical tool's actual method and retain its assumptions. The default method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours. On extended networks, a broad continuous pressure footprint may leave no unaffected neighbours or an overly wide bracket. The pressure-peak-focus fallback can then identify a priority inspection focus from the final five seconds of fully observed paired readings: a unique contiguous pressure-deficit peak, agreeing pairs, independent comparison paths and weaker immediately neighbouring stations whose contrast exceeds the baseline-noise allowance. Missing comparisons, tied/disconnected peaks, inadequate independence and excessive width still withhold a focus. Those comparison stations need not be unaffected. This is a spatial pressure-focus heuristic, not a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem or a guarantee that a physical leak lies inside the interval. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact leak coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or a research formula without its inputs. Physical intervention still requires the approved site procedure and operator authorization.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.
cards.applies_when: An engineer requests a leak location or an inspection recommendation from pressure observations.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived inspection guidance; confirm eligibility and site-specific hydraulic assumptions.
counterexamples: A larger pressure residual is not necessarily the nearest sensor to a leak.
Multiple disjoint pressure regions are not resolved by this single-leak bracket.
verification_steps: Check eligibility, paired coverage, observer independence, actual method and bounding comparisons.
State the priority interval and explain whether its neighbours are unaffected or simply weaker; do not call it a confidence interval or confirmed leak point.
Keep physical confirmation and operator authorization separate from the completed pressure-pattern assessment; do not clear alarms while waiting for an LLM.

cards.title: Expert-guided differential investigation program

sources.boundary: Architecture, expertise capture and open uncertainty/contradiction challenges; no subsea benchmark.

cards.guidance: Use this natural-language program to guide the existing read-only specialist workflow, not to assert an answer. Preserve competing leak, instrumentation and operating explanations. Select measurements and contextual checks that could distinguish them, including counterevidence. Apply only relevant knowledge, explicitly connect it to observed case evidence, and retain contradictions and missing prerequisites. Domain guidance supplies reasoning, not incident facts or authority to clear the numerical warning.
limitations: Inspired by DANA CAPTURE/APPLY and natural-language programs, not an OpenSSA or DanaOS implementation.
The paper's FinanceBench results do not establish pipeline diagnostic accuracy.
cards.applies_when: An anomaly episode requires a bounded, reviewable leak-versus-instrumentation RCA investigation.
cards.review_basis: DANA-inspired investigation program; apply site-reviewed expertise and operator approval.
counterexamples: Retrieving a relevant document without applying it is not RCA.
A well-cited but consistently wrong explanation is not successful expert reasoning.
verification_steps: Quality: establish what was measured reliably and what remains missing.
Diagnosis: inspect connectivity, independent domains and competing signal regions.
Diagnosis: choose relevant operational records and discriminating comparisons.

payload.question: Is this a possible leak or an instrumentation issue? Which pipeline section should an integrity engineer inspect first, and which sensors are unreliable?

cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.
verification_steps: Compare suspect instruments with independent observers and their actual received coverage.
Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

cards.title: Check common causes before counting independent corroboration

sources.boundary: Strong, possible, lower-threshold and noisy detections motivate multiscale inspection; not calibrated gas-pipeline attenuation.
sources.reference: User-provided public defense deck, not redistributed

sources.boundary: Motivates prior knowledge and source-quality review; gateway independence requires site instrumentation verification.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.
Independent gateways do not exclude an unrecorded shared power or operating cause.
verification_steps: Compare near, farther and weak/quiet connected observers jointly, not only above-threshold supporters.
Contrast a shared-path instrument with an independent observer; compare profiles, valid-sample overlap and graph distances.
Inspect contradictory or asynchronous changes rather than merging branch-level earliest/latest timings into a common onset.
Open applicable maintenance records and check effective revision and scope.

cards.title: Test operating transients as competing explanations

sources.boundary: Review of pressure methods, operating transients and model assumptions; not a site-specific operating procedure.

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. Compare the observed sign, timing and affected assets with an approved, incident-time-available record. A proposal is not an executed operation, and a superseded record is not current authority. Read the underlying records referenced by a coverage statement. A plausible explanation for one branch does not automatically explain a different pattern elsewhere. Incomplete logs cannot prove that no operation or leak occurred.
limitations: Temporal association is not a causal intervention.
The cited review includes liquid-pipeline methods; its parameters cannot be transferred directly to subsea gas.
cards.applies_when: Pressure changes could coincide with a valve, compressor, setpoint or calibration activity.
cards.review_basis: Research-grounded guidance; apply the current site operating procedure.
counterexamples: A broad positive operating shift does not by itself explain a separate localized negative region.
A real operating change can coexist with a leak or instrumentation fault.
verification_steps: Search affected and contrasting signal regions, not only the proposed inspection branch.
Open current records and distinguish planned, approved and executed activities.
Compare before/after periods near an observed change; note window censoring and retain missingness.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the numerical tool's actual method and retain its assumptions. The default method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours. On extended networks, a broad continuous pressure footprint may leave no unaffected neighbours or an overly wide bracket. The pressure-peak-focus fallback can then identify a priority inspection focus from the final five seconds of fully observed paired readings: a unique contiguous pressure-deficit peak, agreeing pairs, independent comparison paths and weaker immediately neighbouring stations whose contrast exceeds the baseline-noise allowance. Missing comparisons, tied/disconnected peaks, inadequate independence and excessive width still withhold a focus. Those comparison stations need not be unaffected. This is a spatial pressure-focus heuristic, not a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem or a guarantee that a physical leak lies inside the interval. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact leak coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or a research formula without its inputs. Physical intervention still requires the approved site procedure and operator authorization.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.
cards.applies_when: An engineer requests a leak location or an inspection recommendation from pressure observations.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived inspection guidance; confirm eligibility and site-specific hydraulic assumptions.
counterexamples: A larger pressure residual is not necessarily the nearest sensor to a leak.
Multiple disjoint pressure regions are not resolved by this single-leak bracket.
verification_steps: Check eligibility, paired coverage, observer independence, actual method and bounding comparisons.
State the priority interval and explain whether its neighbours are unaffected or simply weaker; do not call it a confidence interval or confirmed leak point.
Keep physical confirmation and operator authorization separate from the completed pressure-pattern assessment; do not clear alarms while waiting for an LLM.

cards.title: Expert-guided differential investigation program

sources.boundary: Architecture, expertise capture and open uncertainty/contradiction challenges; no subsea benchmark.

cards.guidance: Use this natural-language program to guide the existing read-only specialist workflow, not to assert an answer. Preserve competing leak, instrumentation and operating explanations. Select measurements and contextual checks that could distinguish them, including counterevidence. Apply only relevant knowledge, explicitly connect it to observed case evidence, and retain contradictions and missing prerequisites. Domain guidance supplies reasoning, not incident facts or authority to clear the numerical warning.
limitations: Inspired by DANA CAPTURE/APPLY and natural-language programs, not an OpenSSA or DanaOS implementation.
The paper's FinanceBench results do not establish pipeline diagnostic accuracy.
cards.applies_when: An anomaly episode requires a bounded, reviewable leak-versus-instrumentation RCA investigation.
cards.review_basis: DANA-inspired investigation program; apply site-reviewed expertise and operator approval.
counterexamples: Retrieving a relevant document without applying it is not RCA.
A well-cited but consistently wrong explanation is not successful expert reasoning.
verification_steps: Quality: establish what was measured reliably and what remains missing.
Diagnosis: inspect connectivity, independent domains and competing signal regions.
Diagnosis: choose relevant operational records and discriminating comparisons.
Response: explain which guidance was applied, supporting and contradicting case evidence, and remaining gaps.
Critic: check case facts and knowledge citations against their original pinned sources.
Handoff: request qualified engineer verification; unresolved evidence remains unresolved.

payload.purpose: assess_event_and_location
payload.question: Is this a possible leak or an instrumentation issue? Which pipeline section should an integrity engineer inspect first, and which sensors are unreliable?

cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.
verification_steps: Compare suspect instruments with independent observers and their actual received coverage.
Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

cards.title: Check common causes before counting independent corroboration

sources.boundary: Strong, possible, lower-threshold and noisy detections motivate multiscale inspection; not calibrated gas-pipeline attenuation.
sources.reference: User-provided public defense deck, not redistributed

sources.boundary: Motivates prior knowledge and source-quality review; gateway independence requires site instrumentation verification.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.
Independent gateways do not exclude an unrecorded shared power or operating cause.
verification_steps: Compare near, farther and weak/quiet connected observers jointly, not only above-threshold supporters.
Contrast a shared-path instrument with an independent observer; compare profiles, valid-sample overlap and graph distances.
Inspect contradictory or asynchronous changes rather than merging branch-level earliest/latest timings into a common onset.
Open applicable maintenance records and check effective revision and scope.

cards.title: Test operating transients as competing explanations

sources.boundary: Review of pressure methods, operating transients and model assumptions; not a site-specific operating procedure.

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. Compare the observed sign, timing and affected assets with an approved, incident-time-available record. A proposal is not an executed operation, and a superseded record is not current authority. Read the underlying records referenced by a coverage statement. A plausible explanation for one branch does not automatically explain a different pattern elsewhere. Incomplete logs cannot prove that no operation or leak occurred.
limitations: Temporal association is not a causal intervention.
The cited review includes liquid-pipeline methods; its parameters cannot be transferred directly to subsea gas.
cards.applies_when: Pressure changes could coincide with a valve, compressor, setpoint or calibration activity.
cards.review_basis: Research-grounded guidance; apply the current site operating procedure.
counterexamples: A broad positive operating shift does not by itself explain a separate localized negative region.
A real operating change can coexist with a leak or instrumentation fault.
verification_steps: Search affected and contrasting signal regions, not only the proposed inspection branch.
Open current records and distinguish planned, approved and executed activities.
Compare before/after periods near an observed change; note window censoring and retain missingness.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the numerical tool's actual method and retain its assumptions. The default method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours. On extended networks, a broad continuous pressure footprint may leave no unaffected neighbours or an overly wide bracket. The pressure-peak-focus fallback can then identify a priority inspection focus from the final five seconds of fully observed paired readings: a unique contiguous pressure-deficit peak, agreeing pairs, independent comparison paths and weaker immediately neighbouring stations whose contrast exceeds the baseline-noise allowance. Missing comparisons, tied/disconnected peaks, inadequate independence and excessive width still withhold a focus. Those comparison stations need not be unaffected. This is a spatial pressure-focus heuristic, not a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem or a guarantee that a physical leak lies inside the interval. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact leak coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or a research formula without its inputs. Physical intervention still requires the approved site procedure and operator authorization.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.
cards.applies_when: An engineer requests a leak location or an inspection recommendation from pressure observations.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived inspection guidance; confirm eligibility and site-specific hydraulic assumptions.
counterexamples: A larger pressure residual is not necessarily the nearest sensor to a leak.
Multiple disjoint pressure regions are not resolved by this single-leak bracket.
verification_steps: Check eligibility, paired coverage, observer independence, actual method and bounding comparisons.
State the priority interval and explain whether its neighbours are unaffected or simply weaker; do not call it a confidence interval or confirmed leak point.
Keep physical confirmation and operator authorization separate from the completed pressure-pattern assessment; do not clear alarms while waiting for an LLM.

cards.title: Expert-guided differential investigation program

sources.boundary: Architecture, expertise capture and open uncertainty/contradiction challenges; no subsea benchmark.

cards.guidance: Use this natural-language program to guide the existing read-only specialist workflow, not to assert an answer. Preserve competing leak, instrumentation and operating explanations. Select measurements and contextual checks that could distinguish them, including counterevidence. Apply only relevant knowledge, explicitly connect it to observed case evidence, and retain contradictions and missing prerequisites. Domain guidance supplies reasoning, not incident facts or authority to clear the numerical warning.
limitations: Inspired by DANA CAPTURE/APPLY and natural-language programs, not an OpenSSA or DanaOS implementation.
The paper's FinanceBench results do not establish pipeline diagnostic accuracy.
cards.applies_when: An anomaly episode requires a bounded, reviewable leak-versus-instrumentation RCA investigation.
cards.review_basis: DANA-inspired investigation program; apply site-reviewed expertise and operator approval.
counterexamples: Retrieving a relevant document without applying it is not RCA.
A well-cited but consistently wrong explanation is not successful expert reasoning.
verification_steps: Quality: establish what was measured reliably and what remains missing.
Diagnosis: inspect connectivity, independent domains and competing signal regions.
Diagnosis: choose relevant operational records and discriminating comparisons.
Response: explain which guidance was applied, supporting and contradicting case evidence, and remaining gaps.
Critic: check case facts and knowledge citations against their original pinned sources.
Handoff: request qualified engineer verification; unresolved evidence remains unresolved.

payload.text:
Decision
Work first on P7's shared data connection, gateway-P7-0, serving both sensors at stations ST1, ST3, ST5 and ST7, rather than selecting a pipeline section for leak inspection. Their pressure offset matches the reviewed calibration context; independent comparison stations do not share it. There is no supported joint leak pattern in this window. Next, keep P1-ST6-A and P3-ST7-A on the instrument-check track, P4 and P6 on reading-quality checks, and P2 on operating-context review. P5's current pressure summaries do not support a separate leak priority. A qualified inspection interval is withheld because the P7 affected group lacks independent observers, not because its readings are missing [ev-230; KN-INDEPENDENCE-R1; KN-LOCALIZATION-R1].

Your first actions
1. Scope the P7 review to gateway-P7-0 and its eight named taps; use the already-reviewed calibration record and unaffected ST2/ST4 comparisons to keep this on the instrumentation track.
2. Separate P1-ST6-A's upward drift and P3-ST7-A's downward drift from their stable B partners; flag P4-ST7-B and P6-ST3-A's brief spikes and P6-ST8-B's stuck reading for reading-quality review.
3. Use OP-P2-EXTENDED-001's expected 0.4-bar rise during elapsed recording seconds 90-145 as operating context, not a verified match: the supplied comparisons did not measure P2's transition.
4. Seek independent physical pressure confirmation outside gateway-P7-0 and at P3-ST7, with flow context, to distinguish measurement effects from real pressure loss. These are read-only review decisions, not intervention approval.

Already checked
The focused P7 comparison measured 0.710-0.755-bar downward steps around elapsed second 90; ST2/ST4 changed by only -0.014 to +0.027 bar. Bar is a pressure unit. P7-ST1-A remains 0.720 bar below its supplied normal reference in the final five seconds [ev-194]. P1-ST6-A is instead 3.772 bar above normal, while P3-ST7-A is 3.737 bar below normal; their B partners remain near normal [ev-022; ev-090; comparison 01fae0fc-e079-52a0-a0b4-2ab21fcac667]. These reference differences are not field verification.

Why this decision
Aggregate usable coverage is 99.18%, but health review is partial. P1-ST7-B and P3-ST5-B each lack 20 of 60 expected readings; P4-ST8-A received all 60 but has 15 invalid readings. Neither gaps nor detector flags establish hardware faults [ev-225; ev-027; ev-083; ev-125; KN-QUALITY-R1].

What changes the decision
A sustained loss on independent P7 comparison paths, or independent confirmation of deteriorating pressure at P3-ST7, would raise integrity-review priority. The opened logs are incomplete; they cannot exclude an unrecorded operation or concurrent leak [LOG-EXTENDED-COVERAGE-001; KN-OPERATING-R1].

COMPETING EXPLANATIONS
instrumentation or telemetry (possible): P7's eight odd-station taps show a persistent downward offset beginning around elapsed second 90, confined to one shared data connection. The focused comparison measured approximately 0.75 bar of loss while independent ST2/ST4 stayed nearly unchanged, matching the revised calibration record's expected sign, size and timing. This supports checking the common conversion path rather than declaring eight individual sensors faulty. Association does not establish the cause; confirm gateway assignments and obtain a pressure reference outside that path.

At P1 station ST6, 1100 m along the pipe, sensor A gradually rises while B stays stable; at P3 station ST7, 1300 m along that pipe, A gradually falls while B stays stable. Relative to the supplied normal reference, P1 A/B read respectively 3.635/0.044 bar above normal over the recent 20 seconds and 3.772/0.055 bar above normal in the final five seconds; P3 A reads 3.613 then 3.737 bar below normal, while B reads 0.040 then 0.055 bar above normal. answer.text:
Decision
Work first on P7's shared data connection, gateway-P7-0, serving both sensors at stations ST1, ST3, ST5 and ST7, rather than selecting a pipeline section for leak inspection. Their pressure offset matches the reviewed calibration context; independent comparison stations do not share it. There is no supported joint leak pattern in this window. Next, keep P1-ST6-A and P3-ST7-A on the instrument-check track, P4 and P6 on reading-quality checks, and P2 on operating-context review. Keep P5 on operating-context review because the supplied log contains no verified P5 operating action; this is an evidence gap, not a separate leak finding [LOG-EXTENDED-COVERAGE-001; KN-OPERATING-R1]. A qualified inspection interval is withheld because the P7 affected group lacks independent observers, not because its readings are missing [ev-230; KN-INDEPENDENCE-R1; KN-LOCALIZATION-R1].

Your first actions
1. Scope the P7 review to gateway-P7-0 and its eight named taps; use the already-reviewed calibration record and unaffected ST2/ST4 comparisons to keep this on the instrumentation track.
2. Separate P1-ST6-A's upward drift and P3-ST7-A's downward drift from their stable B partners; flag P4-ST7-B and P6-ST3-A's brief spikes and P6-ST8-B's stuck reading for reading-quality review.
3. Use OP-P2-EXTENDED-001's expected 0.4-bar rise during elapsed recording seconds 90-145 as operating context, not a verified match: the supplied comparisons did not measure P2's transition.
4. Seek independent physical pressure confirmation outside gateway-P7-0 and at P3-ST7, with flow context, to distinguish measurement effects from real pressure loss. These are read-only review decisions, not intervention approval.

Already checked
The focused P7 comparison measured 0.710-0.755-bar downward steps around elapsed second 90; ST2/ST4 changed by only -0.014 to +0.027 bar [comparison subsea_80215fabc7344f68b3b285be473362b5; MAINT-P7-GW-002]. Bar is a pressure unit. P7-ST1-A remains 0.720 bar below its supplied normal reference in the final five seconds [ev-194]. P1-ST6-A is instead 3.772 bar above normal, while P3-ST7-A is 3.737 bar below normal; their B partners remain near normal [ev-022; ev-090; comparison 01fae0fc-e079-52a0-a0b4-2ab21fcac667]. These reference differences are not field verification.

Why this decision
Aggregate usable coverage is 99.18%, but health review is partial. P1-ST7-B and P3-ST5-B each lack 20 of 60 expected readings; P4-ST8-A received all 60 but has 15 invalid readings. Neither gaps nor detector flags establish hardware faults [ev-225; ev-027; ev-083; ev-125; KN-QUALITY-R1].

What changes the decision
A sustained loss on independent P7 comparison paths, or independent confirmation of deteriorating pressure at P3-ST7, would raise integrity-review priority. The opened logs are incomplete; they cannot exclude an unrecorded operation or concurrent leak [LOG-EXTENDED-COVERAGE-001; KN-OPERATING-R1].

competing_causes.text: P7's eight odd-station taps show a persistent downward offset beginning around elapsed second 90, confined to one shared data connection. The focused comparison measured approximately 0.75 bar of loss while independent ST2/ST4 stayed nearly unchanged, matching the revised calibration record's expected sign, size and timing. This supports checking the common conversion path rather than declaring eight individual sensors faulty. Association does not establish the cause; confirm gateway assignments and obtain a pressure reference outside that path.

P7 has measured deficits relative to the supplied normal reference, but agreement among taps on one shared connection is not independent support for a physical leak. P3-ST7-A also reads substantially below normal, yet its paired B reference stays near normal and does not follow the gradual decline. These contradictions prevent a supported joint leak-pattern diagnosis or qualified inspection interval. Independent pressure and flow confirmation could change the assessment; inability to exclude a leak does not itself justify ranking a pipeline section for inspection.

The opened P2 operating record describes an expected positive pressure change of about 0.4 bar during elapsed seconds 90-145. Current P2-ST1 A/B summaries are close to the supplied normal reference, but they do not measure that earlier transition, so a sign, magnitude and timing match has not been demonstrated. That record also does not explain P7's connection-specific negative offset or P3's isolated drift. The coverage record is incomplete and supplies no verified P5 operation; review any additional incident-time operating evidence only if it becomes available.

The focused comparison measured synchronized downward steps of 0.710-0.755 bar around second 90, consistent with the calibration record, not merely a steady deficit with an unknown onset. All eight affected taps share gateway-P7-0, their shared data connection, so agreement between two sensors at each station cannot establish independence or individual hardware faults. Confirm that shared connection against the register and seek an external pressure reference before attributing the cause; no qualified inspection interval is available because the affected group lacks independent observers.

At P1 station ST6, 1100 m along the pipe, sensor A gradually rises while B stays stable; at P3 station ST7, 1300 m along that pipe, A gradually falls while B stays stable. The full-record comparison independently shows opposite A-sensor drifts with little paired agreement, supporting instrument checks rather than joint leak labels. The large departures merit attention but do not confirm faulty hardware; an independent reference at each station would distinguish actual pressure from measurement drift.

P4-ST7-B and P6-ST3-A each have two brief flagged spikes, with observed adjacent jumps of about 2.61 bar; their paired references do not share those excursions. Their final-five-second readings are only 0.047 and 0.011 bar above the supplied normal reference, respectively, so those impulses do not establish sustained pressure loss. P6-ST8-B becomes unchanging in the reviewed profile and has zero pressure range in the current summary, while P6-ST8-A still varies; this is a stuck-reading pattern, not a confirmed hardware cause. Separate coverage gaps affect P1-ST7-B and P3-ST5-B, each missing 20 of 60 expected readings, and P4-ST8-A, with 15 invalid received readings.
